def community_prices_for_wave(t, frames, mode, crop_labels=None):
    """Assemble item-level community_prices for one Nigeria GHS-Panel wave.

    Parameters
    ----------
    t : str
        PH-quarter wave id (e.g. '2011Q1'), used as the `t` index.
    frames : list of dict
        Each dict describes one source price frame:
            df     raw DataFrame (convert_categoricals=False)
            dec    decoded-label DataFrame (for unit / item decode)
            ea     EA id column name (-> v = cluster_id(state, lga, ea))
            state  state column name (default 'state')
            lga    LGA column name   (default 'lga')
            item   item_cd column name
            price  reported-price column name
            unit   unit column name (W3-W5; None for W1/W2)
            size   coded size column (W4 c8q2c, W5 c8aq2_c; None otherwise)
            size_text  free-text size column (W3 c8q2b; None otherwise)
            obs    the form's reading slot this frame records (default 1).
                   W3 is the one wave whose C8 has TWO slots: sectc8a is
                   "C8a: FOOD PRICES - 1ST LOCATION" (obs 1) and sectc8b
                   "C8b: FOOD PRICES - 2ND LOCATION" (obs 2) --
                   PH_W3_Community_Quest.pdf, SECTIONS list "8 Food Prices /
                   a. First location 18 / b. Second location 24"; each
                   section opens with its own location type, name,
                   description, collection date and GPS over the same item
                   list (GH #637 defect C; the GH #840 `obs` contract,
                   lsms_library/data_info.yml Index Info).
    mode : {'codes', 'names'}
        'codes' -> item_cd is the consumption-module scheme already in
                   harmonize_food (W3-W5): resolve via crop_labels (Code).
        'names' -> item_cd is the community questionnaire's own scheme
                   (W1/W2): resolve via _resolve_w1w2_price_item.
    crop_labels : dict, required for mode='codes'
        {int code: Preferred Label} from harmonize_food.

    The C8 form prices "a quantity of ONE (1) [ITEM]" in a stated UNIT and
    SIZE (GH #834): for a coded size carrying a metric quantity (W4/W5 '34.
    250 GRAMS', '24. 75 CL'; W5 also has the c8aq2_a number + c8aq2_cvn kg/l
    factor agreeing with the code), the reported Naira figure is the price
    of THAT PACKAGE, so Price is divided by the decoded quantity and the
    row's unit becomes the metric base unit -- 'g' or 'cl' -- making the
    served number the per-unit price data_scheme.yml documents.  Such rows
    carry the `Derivation` key `Nigeria::community_prices::c8-metric-size`.
    A metric-unit row whose package size is UNRECORDED -- all of W3's
    13,768 g/cl rows bar one (c8q2b is free text, blank on the rest), all
    3,433 of W3's Kg/l rows (the same blank free text, caught only when the
    deletion entry's inputs were written), and W5's 133 rows on '2. GRAMS
    (G)' (c8aq2_c blank) -- is DROPPED: its price is of an unrecorded
    package and per-unit normalization is impossible; serving it under the
    base unit would misprice by the package size (~189x/~42x measured).
    The drop is registered as the deletion entry
    `Nigeria::community_prices::c8-unrecorded-size-drop` (rows: 0 -- a
    dropped row has nowhere to carry a key; `derivation_inputs` returns the
    dropped source rows).  W4 drops NOTHING under this rule: the 1,191 rows
    on raw unit code 1 ('KILOGRAMS (KG)') carry a blank c8q2c, but a blank
    size beside KILOGRAMS is the unremarkable "one kilogram" reading --
    pre-#834 prose that described those rows as a dropped 'Grams(g)' unit
    does not match this read of sectc8_harvestw4.dta.  Ordinal sizes
    (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE, '99.
    ONE SIZE ONLY') carry no metric content: those rows stay under the base
    unit (the size axis remains lost there -- the reported size-specific
    frame is the fix sketched in CONTENTS.org, not adopted).  W1/W2 print
    one unit per item and carry no size columns: unchanged.

    Returns
    -------
    DataFrame indexed by (t, v, j, u, obs) with the `Price` column and,
    where any row was derived, a `Derivation` column (registry key on
    derived rows, NA elsewhere).  `obs` is each frame's reading slot, so
    W3's two locations are two rows, never one selected from the pair
    (GH #637 defect C: until 2026-10-23 the collapse below kept location 1
    in all 2,591 W3 cells both locations priced -- 983 of them at a
    different price -- and served the 3,218 location-2-only rows
    indistinguishable from location 1).

    In 'codes' mode (W3-W5) the key is asserted UNIQUE before the collapse:
    each C8 file is (ea, item_cd)-unique, so a collision would be a broken
    key, not a cell to select from (GH #840).  The Niger duplicate-entry
    drop (a SECOND source record of the same slot that repeats a served
    row) has nothing to act on here -- no W3-W5 file carries a second
    record -- and a W3 location-2 price equal to location 1's is a second
    slot, not a repeat: it is served (Niger's content key includes the
    slot; GhanaLSS serves equal vendor prices).

    'names' mode (W1/W2) still collapses (t, v, j, u, obs=1) duplicates to
    the FIRST price.  That is NOT a dedup of the same surveyed quantity:
    the groups are size variants of one base item (base*10+size codes) and
    distinct items the name map lumps under one label (Maize, Beer, Fish--
    fresh, Butter/Margarine), and most disagree on Price (GH #637 tail
    diagnosis, 2026-10-23: 2,303 of 2,568 W1 groups, 2,605 of 2,951 W2).
    Kept as-is pending a maintainer ruling (a `variety` level, as #840 did
    for Tanzania); see CONTENTS.org.
    """
    DERIVATION_KEY = 'Nigeria::community_prices::c8-metric-size'
    pieces = []
    for fr in frames:
        df = fr['df']
        dec = fr['dec']
        # v must land in the SAME keyspace as sample().v, or a cluster's prices
        # join no households at all.  That means the COMPOSITE (state/lga/ea)
        # id, not the bare `ea` serial (GH #323), and it means building it from
        # raw CODES: `df` here is read with convert_categoricals=False, and the
        # community questionnaire carries no value labels on state/lga anyway,
        # so a label-built key would not match the household side (measured: 0%
        # overlap in W2, 100% on codes).  A community record with no usable EA
        # yields v = None and is dropped by the notna() filter below.
        state_col = fr.get('state', 'state')
        lga_col = fr.get('lga', 'lga')
        v = df.apply(
            lambda r: cluster_id(r.get(state_col), r.get(lga_col), r[fr['ea']]),
            axis=1)
        code = pd.to_numeric(df[fr['item']], errors='coerce')
        price = pd.to_numeric(df[fr['price']], errors='coerce')
        unit_labels = None

        if mode == 'codes':
            j = code.astype('Int64').map(crop_labels).astype('string')
            if fr.get('unit') and fr['unit'] in dec.columns:
                unit_labels = dec[fr['unit']]
                u = unit_labels.map(_canon_community_unit).astype('string')
                initially_unplaced = u.isna()
            else:
                u = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index, dtype='string')
        else:  # names (W1/W2)
            labs, units = [], []
            for c in code:
                if pd.isna(c):
                    labs.append(pd.NA)
                    units.append(pd.NA)
                    continue
                lab, un = _resolve_w1w2_price_item(c)
                labs.append(lab if lab is not None else pd.NA)
                units.append(un if un is not None else pd.NA)
            j = pd.Series(labs, index=df.index, dtype='string')
            u = pd.Series(units, index=df.index, dtype='string')

        piece = pd.DataFrame({
            'v': v.values,
            'j': j.values,
            'u': u.values,
            'obs': int(fr.get('obs', 1)),
            # float64 up-front: the size division below writes non-integer
            # per-unit prices, and a raw int16 price column would refuse
            # them (pandas 3 raises on the silent downcast).
            'Price': price.astype('float64').values,
            'Derivation': pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index,
                                    dtype='string').values,
        }, index=df.index)

        # GH #834 -- the C8 SIZE field.  A coded size carrying a metric
        # quantity means the row's Price is of that PACKAGE, not of one
        # unit: divide through and re-unit to the metric base unit.  A
        # metric-UNIT row whose package size is unrecorded is dropped
        # below (u set to NA here).
        size_col = fr.get('size')
        if size_col and size_col in dec.columns:
            size_lab = dec[size_col].astype('string')
            qty = size_lab.map(_c8_size_metric_grams).astype('Float64')
            is_metric_size = qty.notna()
            # u -> 'g' for gram-coded sizes, 'cl' for cl/litre-coded ones
            is_litre = size_lab.str.contains(r'(?i)\bCL\b|LITRE', na=False)
            metric_u = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index, dtype='string')
            metric_u[is_metric_size & ~is_litre] = 'g'
            metric_u[is_metric_size & is_litre] = 'cl'
            take = is_metric_size & piece['Price'].notna() & (qty > 0)
            piece.loc[take, 'Price'] = piece.loc[take, 'Price'] / qty[take]
            piece.loc[take, 'u'] = metric_u[take]
            piece.loc[take, 'Derivation'] = DERIVATION_KEY
            # A row whose coded unit is metric AND whose size code states a
            # metric quantity has just been re-united to g/cl and divided;
            # it never matches here (its size is recorded).  What remains
            # on g/cl with no size: nothing in W4 (its g/cl unit labels
            # carry a coded size on every row or none -- see
            # _/derivations.yml, c8-unrecorded-size-drop), and in W5 the
            # 133 rows on '2. GRAMS (G)' with a BLANK c8aq2_c.  Exempt the
            # questionnaire's own '99. ONE SIZE ONLY' code.
            one_size = size_lab.str.match(_C8_SIZE_ONE_SIZE_ONLY,
                                          na=False)
            unrecorded = (piece['u'].isin(['g', 'cl'])
                          & size_lab.isna() & ~one_size)
            piece.loc[unrecorded, 'u'] = pd.NA

        size_text_col = fr.get('size_text')
        if size_text_col and size_text_col in df.columns:
            # W3: c8q2b is free text and blank on the whole metric-unit
            # block -- 13,767 of the 13,768 g/cl rows (the 13,768th parses
            # '50cl') and every Kg/l row (2,597 + 836).  Parse the handful
            # that state a quantity ('300gram', 'one 75cl bottle'); the
            # blank remainder is dropped just below.
            txt = df[size_text_col]
            qty = pd.Series(
                [_c8_w3_size_text(x, uu) for x, uu in zip(txt, piece['u'])],
                index=df.index, dtype='Float64')
            take = (piece['u'].isin(['g', 'cl']) & qty.notna()
                    & piece['Price'].notna() & (qty > 0))
            piece.loc[take, 'Price'] = piece.loc[take, 'Price'] / qty[take]
            piece.loc[take, 'Derivation'] = DERIVATION_KEY
            unrecorded = (piece['u'].isin(['g', 'cl', 'Kg', 'l'])
                          & qty.isna())
            piece.loc[unrecorded, 'u'] = pd.NA

        if unit_labels is not None:
            # Report only labels still unplaced AFTER the existing metric
            # rescue.  Reporting up-front falsely counts rescued g/cl rows;
            # known metric units dropped for unrecorded sizes are separate.
            # Retention/fallback remains the explicit #1095 design residual.
            report = (initially_unplaced & piece['u'].isna()
                      & piece['v'].notna() & piece['j'].notna()
                      & piece['Price'].notna() & (piece['Price'] > 0))
            _canon_units(unit_labels[report], canon=_canon_community_unit,
                         where=f'community_prices {t}',
                         disposition='dropped after metric-size rescue')

        pieces.append(piece)

    out = pd.concat(pieces, ignore_index=True)
    out['t'] = t


    # Keep only rows with a resolved cluster, item, unit and a positive
    # price (price 0 / NaN = item not available / not priced; a NA `u`
    # after the size step above is a metric-unit row with an unrecorded
    # package size -- dropped, not served mis-scaled).
    out = out[out['v'].notna() & out['j'].notna() & out['u'].notna()
              & out['Price'].notna() & (out['Price'] > 0)]

    # `obs` is in the key, so W3's two locations are two rows (GH #637
    # defect C).  W3-W5 ('codes') must arrive collision-free: each C8 file is
    # (ea, item_cd)-unique, so a duplicate (t, v, j, u, obs) is a broken key,
    # and the collapse below must not select from it (GH #840).
    key = ['t', 'v', 'j', 'u', 'obs']
    if mode == 'codes':
        dup = out.duplicated(key, keep=False)
        assert not dup.any(), (
            f"community_prices {t}: {int(dup.sum())} rows share a "
            f"{tuple(key)} key -- a broken key, not a cell to select from "
            "(GH #840 / #637)")
    # W1/W2 ('names') only: collapse (t, v, j, u, obs=1) duplicates to the
    # FIRST reported price.  The groups are size variants of one base item
    # and distinct items lumped under one label (see the docstring) -- a
    # SELECTION, kept pending a maintainer ruling, never a cross-cluster
    # aggregate.  `Derivation` is all-NA there (W1/W2 carry no size column),
    # so its `first` is exact; in 'codes' mode every group is one row.
    out = (out.groupby(key, as_index=False)
              .agg({'Price': 'first', 'Derivation': 'first'}))
    if out['Derivation'].isna().all():
        out = out.drop(columns='Derivation')

    # community_prices is a CLUSTER table -- there is no household i, the
    # natural grain is (t, v, j, u, obs).  But the framework's
    # local_tools.map_index() (run on EVERY read path) unconditionally swaps
    # j -> i whenever a `j` index level is present and an `i` level is NOT.
    # That swap would rename our item level `j` to `i`, drop `j`, and collapse
    # the table to (t, v, u).  To keep `j` intact WITHOUT touching the
    # framework, carry a redundant `i` level (set equal to the cluster v)
    # positioned BEFORE `j`: map_index then sees i present and j after i, so it
    # does NOT swap, and the framework's _normalize_dataframe_index drops the
    # undeclared `i` level (data_scheme declares (t, v, j, u, obs)), leaving
    # the declared (t, v, j, u, obs) grain.  v already in the index means
    # _join_v_from_sample is skipped; the spurious i==v never reaches the API.
    # (Same framework-compatibility shim Tanzania/Malawi/Ethiopia/Mali
    # community_prices use.)
    out['obs'] = out['obs'].astype('int64')
    out['i'] = out['v']
    out = out.set_index(['t', 'v', 'i', 'j', 'u', 'obs']).sort_index()
    value_cols = ['Price'] + (['Derivation'] if 'Derivation' in out else [])
    return out[value_cols]
